findings.title: verify never checks session expiry
findings.description: verify returns any session whose token matches, ignoring expiresAt, contradicting its documented contract that expired sessions are rejected.

findings.title: requireAdmin rejects admins
findings.description: allowed.indexOf(session.role) returns 0 for admin, which is falsy, so admin sessions are rejected while owner (index 1) passes.

findings.title: bearerToken crashes on missing/short header
findings.description: Non-null assertions on header and parts[1] dereference undefined input instead of letting handle() return 401.

findings.title: Cache eviction is FIFO, not LRU
findings.description: Eviction picks the first inserted key and never consults the used timestamp, despite docs saying LRU eviction; the used field is recorded but unused.

findings.title: delete leaks the scheduled expiry timer
findings.description: delete removes the entry but neither clearTimeouts its timer nor removes it from timers; timers keep firing and the map grows unbounded.

findings.title: utilization percentage is almost always zero
findings.description: Math.floor(size/limit)*100 floors the ratio before scaling; should scale first. Also divides by zero when limit is 0.

findings.title: keys() returns an empty array
findings.description: for...in over a Map does not enumerate entries, so keys() always returns [].

findings.title: loadConfig mutates the shared DEFAULT_CONFIG
findings.description: cfg is DEFAULT_CONFIG itself, so environment overrides leak into the default object across calls/tests.

findings.title: Invalid timeout is assigned after being logged
findings.description: When LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS is NaN the code logs but still sets cfg.timeoutMs = NaN, and validate doesn't reject NaN.

findings.title: Cache TTL multiplied as if seconds
findings.description: Docs state LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS is in milliseconds, but code multiplies by 1000.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is ignored
findings.description: The parsed limit is validated but never assigned to cfg.fetchLimit.

findings.title: validate always returns true
findings.description: Even when problems are collected, validate returns true, so bad configs are not caught at startup.

findings.title: parseReport emits a trailing empty row
findings.description: Splitting the body leaves a final empty line, which becomes a row with undefined cells.

findings.title: redirect crashes on missing code query
findings.description: Non-null assertion on req.query['code'] throws instead of returning 404 when absent.

findings.title: createLink does not handle invalid JSON
findings.description: JSON.parse can throw on malformed body, surfacing as an unhandled exception rather than a 400 response.

findings.title: stats divides by zero on empty store
findings.description: totalHits()/size() yields NaN when there are no links.

findings.title: report reads a different file than it writes
findings.description: exportCsv defaults an empty name to 'links', but readReport is called with the original empty name, so it reads '.csv' instead of 'links.csv'.

findings.title: create computes quota as NaN
findings.description: this.quota[owner] is undefined initially, so undefined + 1 is NaN and poisons quota counts.

findings.title: resolve deletes non-expired links and never returns them
findings.description: Condition is inverted: links are deleted when Date.now() < expiresAt, so valid links can never resolve; only expired ones fall through to hits++.

findings.title: rename validates from twice and never validates to
findings.description: The second validation repeats from; the destination code 'to' is not validated at all.

findings.title: page end index is off by one
findings.description: When offset+size exceeds length, end is set to all.length + 1; slice clamps, but the intent is all.length.

findings.title: successRate is truncated to 0 unless all links used
findings.description: Math.floor(used/size)*100 floors the ratio before scaling; any partial usage rounds to 0%.

findings.title: delete does not refund the owner's quota
findings.description: Documented behavior refunds the slot, but quota is never decremented.

findings.title: top sorts ascending despite docs
findings.description: Comparator returns positive when a.hits > b.hits, so the least-used links come first.

findings.title: byOwner uses substring match instead of exact owner
findings.description: l.owner.includes(owner) matches any owner containing the string, leaking other owners' links.

findings.title: extend revives expired links
findings.description: Sets expiresAt to now+ttl unconditionally, contradicting the documented finality of expiry for dead codes.

findings.title: quotas returns mutable internal state
findings.description: Documents a snapshot, but returns the live quota object.

findings.title: importAll is not atomic
findings.description: An invalid code mid-batch leaves earlier entries stored, violating the all-or-none contract.

findings.title: prune reports size instead of removed count
findings.description: Function documents the number of removed links but returns this.links.size.

findings.title: expiresAt dereferences possibly missing link
findings.description: Non-null assertion on an entry that may not exist crashes instead of signaling absence.

findings.title: warmCache does not await all probes
findings.description: forEach with async callbacks returns immediately, so warmCache resolves before probing/caching completes and rejections are unhandled.

findings.title: checkTargets runs every probe despite doc
findings.description: Promise.all runs all probes in parallel, not abandoning remaining work after the first failure as documented.

findings.title: flushAudit does not retry until success
findings.description: It calls write() once and ignores the returned promise/retries, contrary to its contract.

findings.title: countForOwner can return NaN
findings.description: quotas[owner] may be undefined, so adding 0 yields NaN for owners without links.

findings.title: Expired/stale timers outlive their cache entries and delete newer ones
findings.description: set() schedules a setTimeout that calls delete(code), but delete() never calls clearTimeout, and set() overwrites the timers map entry without clearing the previous timer. Scenario: an entry for code is set and its timer scheduled; the entry is then deleted and later re-set under the same code with a fresh TTL, so two timers now target the same code. When the original, shorter-lived timer fires it delete()s the newer entry, evicting a live cached value prematurely (and timers keep references, leaking work).

findings.title: warmCache fire-and-forgets its async probes, so it resolves before work finishes
findings.description: warmCache uses pairs.forEach(async ...) and returns void, discarding every returned promise. The caller's await therefore completes before any probe/cache write has finished, and a rejecting probe becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of propagating. Concurrent cache.set writes also interleave with the event loop without any completion guarantee.

findings.title: flushAudit drops the write promise and never retries
findings.description: flushAudit(write) is documented to retry until success but calls write() without awaiting or chaining .then/.catch, and returns void. A rejected write is silently lost as an unhandled rejection, and the 'retried until it succeeds' contract is not implemented, so concurrent/rapid callers cannot tell whether their sync was persisted.

findings.title: checkTargets does not abandon remaining probes after a failure
findings.description: checkTargets awaits Promise.all over every target, so all probes run to completion even after one is known to have failed, contradicting the 'remaining probes are abandoned once a failure is seen' contract. On slow or failing targets this wastes resources and delays reporting the first failure.

findings.title: Janitor interval handle is discarded, so the timer is never cleared
findings.description: startJanitor returns a stopper, but main.ts ignores it. The setInterval therefore runs for the lifetime of the process and cannot be stopped during shutdown or a hot reload, leaking a repeating timer that keeps mutating the store and cache.

findings.title: Hardcoded fallback authentication secret
findings.description: When LINKD_SECRET is unset, the service uses the embedded default secret, so a deployment without that variable shares a known credential value.

findings.title: Session token generated with Math.random
findings.description: Tokens are minted from Math.random() plus a timestamp, so they are neither cryptographically random nor effectively unguessable.

findings.title: Session token logged in full
findings.description: issue() writes the complete bearer token to the console, exposing credentials to anyone with access to logs.

findings.title: verify() never enforces session expiration
findings.description: Sessions set expiresAt, but verify() returns them without checking the time, allowing expired sessions to remain valid indefinitely.

findings.title: requireAdmin authorization check uses indexOf incorrectly
findings.description: allowed.indexOf(session.role) is truthy only at index 1, so the admin role is rejected while owner is accepted, producing unintended authorization behavior.

findings.title: Passwords hashed with fast unsalted SHA-256
findings.description: hashPassword() uses an unmodified SHA-256 hash with no salt, enabling efficient dictionary and rainbow-table attacks against stored digests.

findings.title: bearerToken assumes a present Authorization header
findings.description: The function dereferences an possibly undefined header and crashes on malformed or missing authentication instead of returning a clean auth failure.

findings.title: secretEquals leaks timing information
findings.description: Direct string equality can expose how much of a presented secret matched through timing variation.

findings.title: parseLifetimeHours does not validate numeric input
findings.description: parseInt() can yield NaN or extreme values, allowing malformed or unbounded lifetime requests to propagate into expiry calculations.

findings.title: Invalid timeout value is accepted despite logged validation failure
findings.description: A nonnumeric LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS is logged but still assigned to cfg.timeoutMs as NaN, and validate() always returns true, so the invalid configuration is never rejected.

findings.title: Path traversal through export report name
findings.description: exportCsv() joins a user-controlled name into the target directory without confinement, so ../ segments can write a CSV outside the intended export directory.

findings.title: Export reports written with default file permissions
findings.description: writeFileSync() does not apply the restrictive mode promised in the comment, leaving generated reports readable according to the process umask.

findings.title: Path traversal through owner name in archiveAll
findings.description: archiveAll() uses an owner value directly as a filename component, so an owner such as ../../etc/passwd escapes the export directory.

findings.title: Predictable temporary snapshot path enables overwrite race
findings.description: writeSnapshot() always uses /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json, allowing a local attacker to replace it with a symlink and redirect the write.

findings.title: Path traversal when reading reports
findings.description: readReport() joins a user-controlled name into the directory, allowing ../ segments to read arbitrary paths ending in .csv.

findings.title: Unescaped CSV output allows formula injection
findings.description: Owner and target values are written unquoted, so an owner value beginning with formula characters can execute when the report is opened in spreadsheet software.

findings.title: Permissive CORS combined with credentialed responses
findings.description: The JSON handler advertises Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, an insecure combination for authenticated browser traffic.

findings.title: Client-controlled owner allows ownership spoofing
findings.description: createLink() takes owner from the request body instead of the authenticated session, allowing a caller to create links under another user's identity and quota.

findings.title: Any authenticated user can delete another user's link
findings.description: deleteLink() removes the supplied code without checking that its owner matches the authenticated session, causing unauthorized deletion of other users' links.

findings.title: Open redirect through next query parameter
findings.description: out() redirects directly to the user-supplied next URL without validation, supporting phishing and open-redirect abuse.

findings.title: Admin endpoint guarded only by spoofable header
findings.description: adminQuotas() trusts the client-sent x-admin: true header instead of the authenticated session role, bypassing administrator authorization.

findings.title: Link listing is not scoped to an owner
findings.description: listLinks() returns store results without filtering by the authenticated user, exposing other owners' link data.

findings.title: Report endpoint exports all owners' data without access scoping
findings.description: report() builds its CSV from every link and allows any authenticated user to export data belonging to other owners.

findings.title: Plain object quotas keyed by untrusted owner risk prototype mutation
findings.description: create() uses owner as a dynamic property key on a plain object, so dangerous keys such as __proto__ can mutate object behavior rather than merely storing a quota.

findings.title: Expired link expiry comparison is inverted
findings.description: resolve() deletes links only when the current time is before expiry and leaves expired links resolvable, bypassing link lifetime controls.

findings.title: rename() does not validate the destination code
findings.description: validateCode() is called twice on the source code but never on to, allowing callers to bypass format validation for the destination code.

findings.title: byOwner() matches owners by substring
findings.description: Using includes() instead of equality returns links for all owners whose names contain the query, leaking other owners' data.

findings.title: extend() can revive an expired link
findings.description: The method unconditionally pushes expiry forward even after the link has expired, violating the documented finality of expiry.

findings.title: quotas() exposes the mutable internal object
findings.description: Despite being documented as a snapshot, the method returns the live quota object, allowing recipients to alter stored counts.

findings.title: Short codes use Math.random
findings.description: newCode() relies on non-cryptographic randomness, making generated codes less unpredictable than a cryptographic random source.
